history_operator.domain: Dom(D0) represented on the first-order history graph H1(R)
history_operator.projection: P_X:H->R_X, orthogonal in the declared H metric

necessary_domain_gate.condition: P_X Dom(D0) subset Dom(D0) for every X
necessary_domain_gate.reason: otherwise (I-P_X)D0(I-P_X) is not defined on a common graph domain

uniform_completion_gate.equivalent_estimate: ||D0 P_X h|| <= C(||h||+||D0 h||), uniformly in X
uniform_completion_gate.purpose: control the connection correction -P_XD0-D0P_X+P_XD0P_X on the common graph domain

strong_limit_gate.condition: P_X converges strongly in the graph norm to a projection P_infinity and the compressed forms/operators converge on a common core
strong_limit_gate.result_if_satisfied: D0_dyn,X converges to ((I-P_infinity)D0(I-P_infinity)) tensor I + I tensor A_sep on the stabilized completion

easy_sufficient_case.condition: P_X reduces D0 for every X and the nested projections converge strongly
easy_sufficient_case.consequence: [D0,P_X]=0, graph norm of P_X is at most one, and the compressed diagonal is the direct restriction of D0 to R_X^perp plus separation dynamics on R_X

nonimplication: Hilbert-Schmidt or compact incidence does not imply uniform graph-norm boundedness of its finite range projections; the graph norm sees derivatives and seam traces absent from the ambient L2 projection norm.
cheapest_hostile: compute the largest generalized eigenvalue of the finite Gram pair (G_D0,X,G_H,X), where G_H,X=(<b_p,b_q>) and G_D0,X=(<b_p,b_q>+<D0b_p,D0b_q>); divergence rejects uniform graph completion of P_X
matrix_test: lambda_max(G_H,X^(-1/2) G_D0,X G_H,X^(-1/2)) bounded uniformly in X, interpreted on the nonradical range
disposition: The finite connection has an exact completion criterion. The next executable evidence is a two-Gram generalized-eigenvalue audit of the incidence columns. Current Hilbert-Schmidt summability is insufficient to pass it.
